Translation: Work is carried out with unusual care. The physician finds little to do.
Charm is the house specialty. It pairs well with everything on the menu.
Quick with a retort and quicker to reach for a weapon. This dynasty is remarkably good at handling disagreements — and remarkably good at having them.
They know how to charm a room, fill a tavern, and keep the common folk entertained. Respectable society may call them improper. Usually while trying not to be seen enjoying themselves.
They lost the fortune, not the education. This dynasty can still charm its way through polite society.  Workers, however, tend to find tales of lost privilege somewhat less moving.
Why waste time talking when there's work to be done? A fine philosophy — until someone asks them to make a convincing argument.
Known for their faith, this dynasty has earned the townsfolk's respect. The trouble with being so well regarded is that people notice when you misbehave.
They trust books, experiments, and their own eyes. The faithful may find that troubling, but so far nobody has proven them witches. So far.
A keen eye for advantageous marriages, turning courtship into lasting bonds between houses.
Disciplined and difficult to catch unprepared. Thieves know better than to linger near their property. Diplomacy is useful, certainly. They simply prefer something a little more… convincing.
Hard-earned new money spends just as well as old money. Those who inherited theirs may disagree. Apparently, wealth is more respectable when your grandfather had it first.

A famous name, impeccable manners, and not a callus in sight. This dynasty moves with ease through political circles — just don't expect its well-kept descendants to fare quite as gracefully in a fight.
Allies, rivals, principles — useful things, provided you know when to set them aside. This family has survived by keeping its options open.
A life close to crime has made this dynasty tough, discreet, and quick to learn the tricks of the trade. The guards have every reason to be wary.
Bad things have a habit of happening around this family. The stranger part is how often they survive them. After a while, people start drawing conclusions.
Worn and creaky, but still serviceable — mostly.

Swept floors, polished counters, and not a single rat in sight.

A few petty acts here and there — nothing that shakes the quarter's peace.

The streets are safe, patrols are steady, and the people sleep well.

Disheveled hair and a certain satisfied glow. A well-tended marriage leaves its marks.
Some of us are simply… better.

Overcome by fear. Unable to act against the one who caused it.

Hard to work when the insides want out.
A philosopher's death — wasted on this one.

The rash is only the beginning.

Blisters swell with infected fury, each bursting into raw, weeping sores that only deepens the agony.

Four walls, one fate. And far too much time to regret what brought you here.
Time slows down here. No creaks, no cracks, no worries.
Stonework so precise, carts glide through untouched. Not a jolt, not a scratch.
Your name travels faster than you do—and rarely for the right reasons.
Wounded and slowed. Every task takes longer, every step comes with pain.
The food was fine. The speech? That changed something.
A visible sign of wealth and standing.
Gone for now. Possibly fed. Probably priced.
A harsh hit sent them to the ground. Getting up will take time — or help.
A visible armed presence. Keeps the streets calmer — and the criminals twitchy.
If everyone is laughing, surely they earned it.
Music spills into the street. Crowds gather — best keep the beer stocked.
Recent storms turned the road to sludge. Carts crawl, wheels groan, and nothing moves quickly.
Revived by a forbidden deal. Still walking. Technically dead.
Completely immobilized. Still conscious, and unfortunately aware.
